statement: Records can be exchanged with international and allied DCAT-based profiles without bespoke translation for each pair.
rationale: Every bespoke translation is a cost and a place where meaning is lost.
acceptance: For each listed profile, a crosswalk exists and a round trip through the weaver keeps every mandatory value.
gap: Crosswalks cover CKAN, Dublin Core, UK GEMINI, HDR UK, Croissant and DDI, and the weaver also reads and writes DCAT-US and schema.org. Allied profiles that are not public are out of scope here.

statement: Finding a record never grants access to the data. Who may have the data is stated separately from who may see the record.
rationale: Discovery across government only works if publishing a record does not expose the data.
acceptance: Datasets and data services carry access rights; catalogue records carry their own audience.
validation: SHACL and JSON Schema shapes for accessRights and metadataAudience

statement: A catalogue record can say how the record itself must be handled, separately from the handling of the data it describes.
rationale: A record about protected data is often itself OFFICIAL, and a shared catalogue needs to know that.
acceptance: Catalogue records take a security classification of their own, from the same list as datasets.
validation: Generated shapes for CatalogueRecord; class page diagram

statement: A record can say why a property is empty (unknown, withheld, not applicable, not collected or not yet available), so a strict harvester need not guess.
rationale: Stricter validators treat an absent value as an error. An explicit reason lets them tell a withheld value from a forgotten one.
acceptance: Missing values are structured, use a controlled list of reasons, and never satisfy a mandatory property (rule Q-02).
validation: tests/test_toolkit.py MissingValues; tests/fixtures/invalid.yaml missing-value-bad-reason and missing-value-no-reason

statement: Validation is machine-readable and gives one verdict wherever it runs.
rationale: A record that passes in one tool and fails in another cannot be trusted by either.
acceptance: pySHACL, JSON Schema and validator.js agree on every example and every deliberate break.
validation: tests/test_profile.py every example passes all three; every break fails all three

statement: Conformance is claimed by level and by layer, and only after the matching tests pass.
rationale: A single yes or no hides what a catalogue can actually exchange.
acceptance: The conformance kit gives levels 1 to 3 for the core. Each further layer gets its own test records before anyone may claim it.
gap: Levels exist for the core only. Layer claims (data asset management, sectors, controlled overlays) are planned.

statement: Specialist terms live in their own namespaces, as modules that can be required or left out as a whole.
rationale: Modules let a community be strict about its own terms without making everyone else carry them.
acceptance: Each extension is a module with its own mandatory and optional properties, using its sector's vocabulary, merged by one function.
validation: Profile.with_extensions; extension tests in check_browser (break extension)
gap: Extensions reuse their sectors' namespaces. New UK-only terms still go in the one dcatuk namespace; a namespace per module is not yet decided.

statement: The authoritative source of a record, and of each value changed on the way, survives harvesting and mapping.
rationale: Enriched or merged records that look like the original mislead people about who is accountable.
acceptance: Records carry publisher, creator and qualified attribution; harvested copies keep the original identifier, point to the record they came from (source record) and list the properties they enriched.
validation: Generated shapes; weaver notes; worked example record-harvested

statement: Every mapping says what it loses.
rationale: Silent loss is worse than visible loss.
acceptance: The weaver returns notes on values it changes or drops, and the crosswalk matrix marks partial and missing matches.
gap: Notes are written by hand for each reader and writer, so a new mapping could drop a value without a note. A generic loss report is planned.

statement: Asset, dataset, data product, data service and distribution have one meaning each, which policy and catalogues share.
rationale: Departments reporting under the same policy count different things when the words differ.
acceptance: Each term has a definition, a class or a stated mapping to one, and an entry in the glossary.
gap: Data product has no class of its own and no agreed mapping yet.

statement: Organisations without an enterprise catalogue can still describe their assets, from a spreadsheet, and be found.
rationale: Discovery should not wait for every department to buy a catalogue.
acceptance: The bulk checker reads a spreadsheet (CSV) and gives a verdict for every row.

statement: The profile works with the catalogue platforms departments already run, through configuration or adapters.
rationale: Replacing platforms to adopt a standard is the lock-in the standard is meant to prevent.
acceptance: Each named platform has an integration pattern and a test route through the conformance kit.
gap: Product entries are background knowledge until each supplier confirms them (open register O-19).

statement: Validation works in disconnected and air-gapped environments, with no calls to the network.
rationale: Many protected environments cannot reach the internet.
acceptance: The validator, its profile file and the command line run offline; validator.js makes no network calls.

statement: The public profile describes OFFICIAL information only. Anything needing higher classifications is handled in controlled layers.
rationale: An OFFICIAL catalogue must not become a list of protected holdings.
acceptance: The security classification guidance says records about SECRET or TOP SECRET data do not belong in an OFFICIAL catalogue; the portal carries no protective markings.

statement: Where allied exchange needs it, DCAT-AP-UK maps to the NATO Core Metadata Specification and its confidentiality labelling.
rationale: Defence data shared with allies is described in NATO's own core metadata.
acceptance: A mapping reviewed against authorised sources. No conformance claim is made until then.

statement: Geospatial records reference GEMINI rather than repeat it.
rationale: Two sources of truth for the same geospatial terms drift apart.
acceptance: The geospatial extension is aligned to GeoDCAT-AP and UK GEMINI, with a crosswalk to GEMINI, and defines nothing they already define.
gap: Review of the crosswalk by geospatial specialists is planned.

statement: Catalogues and information asset registers work together without becoming two registers of the same things.
rationale: Duplicate registers disagree, and people stop trusting both.
acceptance: A stated mapping between register fields and DCAT-AP-UK properties, tested on a real register extract.

statement: Public artefacts never expose controlled semantics, and never name people or meetings from internal engagement.
rationale: Openness is the default, but aggregation can reveal what single facts do not.
acceptance: A check fails the build if requirements or pages carry protective markings or controlled-specification terms.

statement: Missing metadata is collected from the business areas that hold it, without a central team re-keying it.
rationale: Departments often do not hold all the metadata centrally.
acceptance: Guidance and a bulk route for business areas to supply and verify their own entries.
gap: The bulk checker exists; the commissioning guidance does not.

statement: Policing and justice systems can describe shared data with the same core, alongside their own interoperability layers.
rationale: Interoperability in policing is organised in layers that a common metadata core can sit inside.
acceptance: A worked mapping from the core to the semantic layer of policing interoperability guidance.

statement: Metadata held in a catalogue platform's own model, such as the Apache Atlas types behind Microsoft Purview, converts to DCAT-AP-UK through a mapping layer, not by re-keying.
rationale: Departments adopting a platform should not have to choose between its tooling and cross-government discovery.
acceptance: The weaver reads Atlas v2 entities, turns epoch times into dates, keeps GUIDs only as identifiers, and names every DCAT-AP-UK property the entity cannot supply.

statement: A mapping never invents a value. No default description, licence, language, contact name or classification; a missing value stays missing and is reported.
rationale: A plausible default is worse than a gap, because nobody goes back to check it. Defaulting an unlabelled asset to OFFICIAL is a security decision nobody made.
acceptance: No reader in the weaver sets a value the source does not hold; each gap becomes a note.

statement: Precise positions say which reference frame and epoch they are in, how they were observed and how uncertain they are, at a stated confidence.
rationale: The same point has different coordinates in different frames and at different dates; mixing them silently is an error of centimetres to metres.
acceptance: A geodesy module with frame, epoch, vertical reference, technique and uncertainty with confidence, and deliberate breaks.
gap: A candidate for review by geodetic specialists. Rules linking uncertainty to confidence, and frame to epoch, are not yet enforced.

statement: Geospatial records state their coordinate reference system, give resolution with a unit, and say how the data is represented; geospatial services state the OGC standards they conform to.
rationale: These are the facts a geospatial user checks first, and the ones generic discovery metadata leaves out.
acceptance: Shapes in the geospatial extension for each of the four, with deliberate breaks.
validation: Extension breaks geo-without-crs and geo-bad-representation; a data service without conforms to fails under the extension

statement: A record declares which profile, layers and versions it was written to.
rationale: A harvester cannot apply the right rules, or migrate a record, if it does not know which ones it was made against.
acceptance: Catalogue records give the profile and each layer as versioned identifiers in conforms to.
validation: Generated shapes for CatalogueRecord; worked example record-harvested
gap: The property exists, but there is no published identifier per layer version yet, and no rule checks that the identifier is a known one.

statement: A release passes four gates. Reuse is assessed for every new term; every rule is traced to a test; no serious semantic-loss or disclosure defect is open; compatibility is claimed only with evidence.
rationale: Gates make "ready" a fact anyone can check rather than an opinion.
acceptance: Each gate has a check in the release workflow or a recorded decision, shown on this page.
gap: Traceable tests and the defect register are enforced; reuse assessment is recorded per property but not as a gate, and semantic-loss defects are not graded by severity.

statement: UK profiles agree which properties are mandatory, recommended and optional, so a record that conforms to one is not rejected by another.
rationale: Profiles built for statistics and for cross-government catalogues drifted apart on obligations, so the same record passed one and failed the other.
acceptance: A published comparison of obligations with each UK profile, and a decision on every difference.

statement: Every requirement can be followed from its evidence to the properties, rules, tests, decisions and release that meet it.
rationale: A requirement that cannot be traced cannot be shown to be met, or safely changed.
acceptance: The lineage explorer links each requirement to what traces it; the chain below counts each link.
validation: tests/test_integrations.py RequirementsStream every requirement is in the lineage
gap: Decisions and releases are not yet linked to individual requirements in the lineage.

statement: Partner overlays attach to the core without changing it. Core discovery stays open; overlay terms apply only in partner exchanges.
rationale: Loading partner controls onto the civil core would make it harder to adopt and leak semantics that should stay controlled.
acceptance: A controlled overlay specified, tested and governed outside this repository, using only the extension points the core publishes.
